chunks: Al-Husayn ibn al-Husayn said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamadani narrated to us, Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Abdi narrated to us, and I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:

Fasting on the Day of Ghadir Khumm is equal to the fasting of a lifetime; if a person lived and then fasted for the duration of their life, they would receive the reward of that. Their fasting is equal in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in each year to one hundred accepted and accepted Hajj pilgrimages and one hundred accepted and accepted Umrah pilgrimages. And it is the Greatest Eid of Allah.

And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, never sent a Prophet but he celebrated this day and recognized its sanctity. Its name in the heavens is the Day of the Covenant Promised, and on earth it is the Day of the Covenant Taken and the Gathering Witnessed.

Whoever prays two rak'ahs in it, performing ghusl at the decline of the sun before it declines, for the duration of half an hour, asking Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reciting Surah al-Hamd once in each rak'ah, and ten times 'Qul huwa Allahu Ahad', and ten times the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), and ten times 'Inna anzalnahu'.

It is equal in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to one hundred thousand Hajj pilgrimages and one hundred thousand Umrah pilgrimages. And whatever he asks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of the needs of this world and the hereafter, it will be granted, whatever the need may be.
And if the two rak'ahs and the supplication are missed by you, you can make them up afterwards.
And whoever feeds a believer on this day is like one who fed a multitude, and a multitude, and a multitude. He will continue to be counted until he ties ten with his hand.

Then he said: Do you know how many are the multitudes? I said: No. He said: One hundred thousand. Each multitude has the reward of one who feeds, by their number, 'from the Prophets and the Truthful and the Martyrs' in the sanctuary of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
And gave them drink 'on a day of thirst', and the dirham in it is worth a thousand thousand dirhams.
He said: Perhaps you think that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created a day greater in sanctity than it? No, by Allah, no, by Allah, no, by Allah.

And let it be from your speech when you meet each other that you say: Praise be to Allah who honored us with this day and made us among those who fulfill His covenant with us and His pledge with which He guaranteed to us the guardianship of the leaders of His affair and those who establish justice.
And did not make us among those who deny and those who falsify the Day of Judgment.

Then he said: And let it be from your supplication after these two rak'ahs that you say: 'Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], Believe in your Lord, so we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous. Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise.'

Then you say after that: O Allah, I bear witness to You, and sufficient is You as a Witness, and I bear witness to Your angels and the bearers of Your Throne and the inhabitants of Your heavens and Your earth that You are Allah, the One worshipped, who is not from near Your Throne to the settlement of Your earth any worshipped worshipped besides You except falsehood fading, other than Your Noble Face. No god is worshipped besides You. Exalted are You above what the oppressors say, a great elevation.

And I bear witness that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is Your servant and Your Messenger, and I bear witness that Ali (peace be upon him) is the Commander of the Faithful, their guardian and their master.

Our Lord, indeed we heard the call and confirmed the caller, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he called with a call from You regarding what You commanded him to convey regarding the guardianship of the leader of Your affair, so You warned him and notified him that if he does not convey, You will be displeased with him, and that if he conveys Your messages, You will protect him from the people.

So he called, conveying Your revelation and Your messages: Behold, whoever I am his master, Ali is his master, and whoever I am his guardian, Ali is his guardian, and whoever I am his prophet, Ali is his commander.

Our Lord, so we have answered Your caller, the Warner, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), Your servant and Your Messenger, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) whom You favored and made an example for the Children of Israel, indeed he is the Commander of the Faithful, their master and their guardian until the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Judgment.

Indeed You said: 'He is not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made an example for the Children of Israel.' Our Lord, we believed and followed our master and our guardian and our guide and our caller and the caller of mankind, and Your straight path, the upright one, and Your proof and Your way calling to You with clear insight. He and whoever follows him, and 'Glory be to Allah from what they associate [with Him]'.

By his guardianship and by what they deviate by taking guardians besides him. So I bear witness, O my God, that he is the Imam, the Guide, the Rightly Guided, Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, whom You mentioned in Your book and said: 'And indeed he is in the Mother of the Book with Us, Ali, the Wise'.

I do not associate with him any Imam, nor do I take from him any guardian. O Allah, indeed we bear witness that he is Your servant, the Guide after Your Prophet, the Warner, the straight path, the Commander of the Faithful, the leader of the brightly shining, Your reaching proof, Your tongue expressing for You among Your creation, and the one establishing justice after Your Prophet, and the judge of Your religion, and the keeper of Your knowledge, and the place of Your secret, and the container of Your knowledge, and Your trustworthy one whose pledge is taken with the pledge of Your Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) from all Your creation and beings.

A testimony of sincerity to You in monotheism, that You are Allah, there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, and Ali is the Commander of the Faithful, and that confession to his guardianship is the completion of Your monotheism and sincerity in Your oneness and the perfection of Your religion and the completion of Your favor and grace upon all Your creation and beings.
Indeed You said, and Your word is the truth: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.'

O Allah, to You is the praise for what You bestowed upon us of sincerity to You in Your oneness, when You guided us to the allegiance of Your guardian, the Guide, after Your Prophet, the Warner, and You approved for us Islam as a religion through his allegiance, and You completed upon us Your favor which You renewed for us Your covenant and pledge, and reminded us of that, and made us among the people of sincerity and confirmation of Your covenant and pledge, and among the people of fulfillment of that.

And You did not make us among those who break [covenants] and deny and falsify the Day of Judgment, and You did not make us among the followers of those who change and alter and deviate and make deaf the ears of livestock, and those who change the creation of Allah, and among those 'whom Satan has seized and made them forget the remembrance of Allah' and turned them from the path and from the straight path.
And increase in your saying on your day and night that you say: O Allah, curse the deniers and the breakers and the changers and the falsifiers of the Day of Judgment from the first and the last.

O Allah, to You is the praise for Your bestowing upon us by which You guided us to the guardianship of the leaders of Your affair after Your Prophet, the guiding, rightly guided Imams, whom You made pillars for Your monotheism and signs of guidance and beacons of piety and the firmest handhold and the perfection of Your religion and the completion of Your favor.

To You is the praise. We believed in You and confirmed Your Prophet and followed after him the Warner, and we affirmed their guardian and opposed their enemy, and we are free from the deniers and the breakers and the falsifiers until the Day of Judgment.

O Allah, as it is Your way, O Truthful of the Promise, O He 'who does not break the promise', O He who is every day in a matter, that You bestowed upon us the allegiance of Your guardians, for which Your servants will be asked. Indeed You said, and Your word is the truth: 'Then you will surely be asked that Day about the favor.' And You said: 'And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned.'

And You bestowed upon us the testimony of sincerity to You through the allegiance of Your guiding guardians after the Warner, the Warner, and the shining lamp, and You perfected the religion through their allegiance and the expulsion of their enemy, and You completed upon us the favor which You renewed for us Your covenant and reminded us of Your pledge taken from us at the beginning of Your creation of us.

And You made us among the people of response, and You reminded us of the covenant and the pledge, and You did not make us forget Your remembrance. Indeed You said: 'And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify against themselves, [saying], Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes.'

O Allah, yes, we testified by Your grace and kindness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, our Lord, and Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, our Prophet, and Ali is the Commander of the Faithful, and the Great Proof, and Your Great Sign, and the Great News 'about which they differ'.

O Allah, as it is Your way that You bestowed upon us guidance to their knowledge, let it be Your way that You send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You bless us in this day in which You reminded us of Your covenant and pledge, and perfected our religion, and completed upon us Your favor, and made us among the people of response and sincerity in Your oneness, and among the people of faith and confirmation of the guardianship of Your guardians and the expulsion of Your enemies and the enemies of Your guardians, the deniers and the falsifiers of the Day of Judgment.

And that You do not make us among the erring, and do not join us with the falsifiers of the Day of Judgment, and make for us a firm footing with the Prophets, and make for us with the pious an Imam until the Day of Judgment, the day when every 'group will be called by their Imam'.

And gather us in the group of the guided, the rightly guided, and keep us alive as long as You keep us alive upon fulfillment of Your covenant and pledge taken from us and upon us for You, and make for us with the Messenger a way, and make firm for us a footing of truth in the migration.

O Allah, make our life the best of lives and our death the best of deaths, and our return the best of returns, until You cause us to die while You are pleased with us, having obligated for us the dwelling of Your Paradise by Your mercy, and the abode in Your house, and the return to the House of Permanence from Your grace.

'No weariness will touch them therein, nor will they touch it with exhaustion.' Our Lord, indeed You commanded us to obey the leaders of Your affair, and You commanded us to be with the truthful. So You said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you.' And You said: 'Fear Allah and be with the truthful.'

So we heard and obeyed, our Lord, so 'Make firm our feet' and 'Cause us to die as Muslims', confirming Your guardians, and 'Do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'

O Allah, I ask You by the truth which You made with them and by which You favored them over all the worlds, that You bless us in this day in which You honored us, and that You complete upon us Your favor, and make it with us permanent, and do not deprive us of it forever, and do not make it deposited. Indeed You said: 'So permanent and deposited.' So make it permanent and do not make it deposited.

And grant us the victory of Your religion with a guiding, victorious guardian from the family of Your Prophet, and make us with him and under his banner truthful martyrs in Your cause and for the victory of Your religion.
Then you ask after it your need for this world and the hereafter, for indeed it, by Allah, is granted on this day.

key_terms.اَلنَّذِيرِ: The Warner, a title for the Prophet Muhammad.
key_terms.اَلْإِخْلَاصِ: Sincerity, referring to pure monotheism and devotion.
key_terms.اَلْعَهْدِ اَلْمَعْهُودِ: The Promised Covenant, a heavenly name for the Day of Ghadir.
key_terms.اَلْمِيثَاقِ: The Pledge, referring to the covenant taken from humanity or specifically from the Prophet and Imams.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two rak'ahs, referring to the specific prayer of Ghadir.
key_terms.صِيَامُ: Fasting, specifically referring to the fast of Ghadir.
key_terms.غَدِيرِ خُمٍّ: Ghadir Khumm, the location where the Prophet Muhammad announced the Imamate of Ali.
key_terms.وِلَايَةِ: Guardianship/Authority, referring to the spiritual and political authority of the Imams.

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and ritual prayers of fasting on the Day of Ghadir Khumm according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes Ghadir Khumm as the 'Eid of Allah' and the day of the 'Great Covenant,' where the fasting reward equals a lifetime of worship, underscoring its status as the completion of the divine religion. The hadith prescribes a specific two-rak'ah prayer with precise recitations and supplications, linking the theological concept of Wilayah to the practical act of worship, thereby making the acceptance of all worldly and spiritual needs contingent upon this devotion. This narrative serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence regarding the ritual observance of the 18th of Dhu al-Hijjah, emphasizing both gratitude for the covenant and the necessity of affirming Ali's authority as the seal of prophethood's guidance.
